svg.title: AgentGlass animated explainer
svg.desc: A looping seven-chapter motion graphic explaining agent execution tracing, event schema, spans and tool calls, best-effort redaction, local JSONL storage, CLI inspection, and the difference between shipped and planned features. Synthetic example data only.

g.text: A final answer hides the path.
An agent may call models, run tools, retry work, or fail before it responds.
You see the answer — not the execution history.
so builders can inspect what ran, when, and why a step failed.
Turn activity into an event timeline.
Your application records the events it can actually observe.
Run lifecycle · model hooks · tool input/output · errors · explicit custom events
Every event has a predictable shape.
A versioned contract makes traces easier to validate, store, and compare.
Provider-specific usage data is only recorded
when an integration actually supplies it.
Spans and tool events carry measured duration and links to their start event.
One parent run contains nested operations
parent_event_id links the terminal event to its start
input and output metadata may be captured
Timing is measured around the instrumented operation; it is not a performance benchmark.
PARENT LINKS · OPERATION TIMING · FAILURE CONTEXT
Redact before the event is stored.
The default redactor masks common sensitive keys and recognizable token/email patterns.
Avoid collecting sensitive data at source.
Important: pattern-based redaction is not a complete DLP guarantee.
Review traces before sharing them; local files may still contain confidential context.
Keep the trace local. Inspect it from the CLI.
Use a test-friendly memory store or append structured events to a JSON Lines file.
No hosted collector in this MVP
Also available: agentglass validate PATH · agentglass summary PATH
The demo trace is synthetic and makes no external model/API calls.
A real tracing core. A clear roadmap.
The product status is explicit: implemented functionality is separated from planned work.
○ Interactive dashboard with real trace files
Next: instrument one real workflow and inspect the events it produces.
Start with the offline demo, then replace synthetic data with explicit application observations.
AGENTGLASS · OBSERVE WHAT HAPPENED. TRACE WHAT FAILED.
